submission.natural_language_explanation: Two related triggers in news-style prose. (1) Violent-conflict reporting: tokens inside or right after a clause about killing, attacks, bombs, shootings, coups, uprisings or epidemics (e.g. 'killed in [a]', 'attack in Paris [killed]', 'the [Ebola]') fire strongly, typically 1.5-3.6. (2) The first sub-token of a rare multi-token proper noun or foreign word whose completion is not yet determined (' McL'emore, ' Bur'undi, ' An'bar, ' int'ifada, ' Kirst'i, Gany'med'e, ' Tem'el) fires 1-3.2 even in neutral context, and more in conflict or sports news. Single-token common names and words (Smith, Jones, Kenya, Mary) in neutral everyday text, code and generic prose stay near 0 on every token, so no floor applies.
